title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation [the process of becoming like Jesus] part 3
devotional:
How are we to understand the image of God?

The Image of God is not something you have, it is something much more profound, it is something you are, something you have been made into, it is the very essence of who we are. There has been a lot of debate as to what the term actually means, this debate has caused much confusion and I think has added to a lack of understanding about who we are.

Most Christians believe in what is known as the substantive view of the image of God, which means we are spiritually and physiologically similar to God. So God is rational, creative, he is moral knowing the difference between right and wrong. He has the ability to choose good or bad, unlike all other creatures, humankind have these qualities to a greater degree. This sounds very reasonable. However, there are a number of problems with this understanding.

a. Some animals can be rational.

Cameron Buckner, Assistant Professor of Philosophy at the University of Houston, argues in an article published in Philosophy and Phenomenological Research, that a wide range of animal species exhibit so-called “executive control” when it comes to making decisions, consciously considering their goals and ways to satisfy those goals before acting. He acknowledges that language is required for some sophisticated forms of meta cognition, or thinking about thinking. But bolstered by a review of previously published research, Buckner concludes that a wide variety of animals – elephants, chimpanzees, ravens and lions, among others – engage in rational decision-making.

b. Can animals be moral?

Eleanor, the matriarch of her family, is dying and unable to stand. Grace manages to lift her to her feet. She tries to get Eleanor to walk, pushing her gently along. But Eleanor falls again. Grace appears very distressed, and shrieks loudly. She persists in trying to get Eleanor to stand, unsuccessfully. Grace stays by the fallen figure of Eleanor for another hour, while night falls. If Grace were human, we might have little hesitation in attributing to her an emotion of a certain sort: compassion or sympathy. But neither Grace nor Eleanor is human. Eleanor is the matriarch of the First Ladies family of elephants. Grace is a younger member of another family of elephants.

Ian Douglas Hamilton, Bhalla, S., Wittemyer, G. & Vollrath, F., “Behavioural Reactions of Elephants Towards a Dying and Deceased Matriarch.” Applied Animal Behaviour Science 100, (2006), 67-102.

c. Satan, demons and angels, are creative, are moral, knowing the difference between right and wrong, and have the ability to choose good or bad. Does that mean they are created in the image of God?

d. What about people who are cognitively impaired?

Those who have intellectual disabilities and restricted in the capacity to reason or do not have the necessary moral facilities to build relationships are they less than human? Are they not created in the image of God?

That is what Hitler believed, so he had death camps build to exterminate non Aryan’s, not only Jews, but those with physical and mental disabilities.

Hitler set up a committee of physicians to prepare for the murder of mentally and physically disabled children. Known as the Reich Committee for the Scientific Treatment of Severe Hereditary and Congenital Diseases, the group was told to keep its mission secret. In August 1939, committee members asked doctors and midwives to fill out a questionnaire that would identify children born with various deformities or disabilities. Initially, the focus was on children under the age of three. The committee claimed it was using the information “to clarify certain scientific questions.” In fact, it was used to determine which children would be allowed to live. The committee relied entirely on the questionnaires in making its decisions. Members did not examine a single child, consult with other physicians, or speak to the families involved. Once a decision was made, the committee told the child’s parents only that their baby was being placed in a special hospital to “improve” treatment. There, death came quickly. After the war, a physician involved in the program told Robert Jay Lifton, an American psychiatrist, “According to the thinking of that time, in the case of children, killing seemed somehow justifiable whereas in the case of the adult mentally ill, that was definitely murder.” ‘Unworthy to live,’’ Holocaust and human behaviour. Chapter 8. Facinghistory.org

5. In the creation story and the rest of the Hebrew bible there are many similarities between mankind and the rest of the animal kingdom.

Created [Hebrew word bara] used for Humans Genesis 1:27, Malachi 2:10

Animals Genesis 1:27, Psalm 110:30

Made [Hebrew word asah] used for Humans Genesis 1:26

Animals Genesis 1:25

Soul [Hebrew word nephesh] used for Humans Genesis 2:7, 9:5, 12:5

Animals Genesis 1:20,30, 2:19, 9:4

Spirit [Hebrew word neshamah] used for Both Genesis 6:17, 7:22

Spirit of life

[Hebrew words rauch hayuyim] used for Humans Genesis 2:7, 9:5

Animals Genesis 1:20-24, 2:19,

9:10,15.

Flesh [Hebrew word basar] used for Humans Genesis 2:7, 9:5.

Animals Genesis 41:2-19,

Exodus 21:28

These similarities means that it is important that we have a proper understanding of what it means to be made in God’s image, because the image of God is the thing that ultimately defines us from the rest of creation.
prayer: Father thank you that being made in your image is a lot more than having moral capacities.
